title: Product of Array Except Self
statement: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer where answer[i] is the product of every element of nums except nums[i]. You must run in O(n) time and you may NOT use the division operator. The output array does not count towards extra space.
realWorld: Leave-one-out weighting shows up wherever a combined score must be recomputed without one contributor: the end-to-end success rate of a pipeline if one stage were removed, or the joint probability of a set of independent signals with one signal held out for scoring. Division is exactly the wrong tool there, because a single zero — a stage that failed every request — is the case you most want an answer for.

examples.explanation: answer[0] = 2*3*4 = 24, answer[1] = 1*3*4 = 12, and so on. Note 24 = (everything left of index 0, which is nothing, so 1) * (everything right of it, 24).
Every position except index 2 has the zero somewhere in its product, so it is 0. Index 2 excludes the zero and gets (-1)*1*(-3)*3 = 9. This is the case that kills the divide-the-total shortcut.

constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix of nums fits in a 32-bit integer
Division is not allowed; the required time is O(n)

bruteForce.idea: For each index, multiply every other element together.
bruteForce.whySlow: The product for index i multiplies the whole block nums[0..i-1] that index i-1 has just finished multiplying, and the block nums[i+1..n-1] that index i+1 is about to multiply again. Each element is multiplied n-1 separate times, although it only ever contributes two facts to the entire answer: the product of everything before it and the product of everything after it. Those two families of products are each n numbers long and each takes one pass to build.

patternIdentification: answer[i] depends on 'everything to the left of i' and 'everything to the right of i'. Whenever that is the shape, build the two families of running aggregates once — a left-to-right sweep and a right-to-left sweep — and combine them per index. The ban on division is what forces the shape into view, and it is also what makes the result survive zeros: nothing is ever undone, only accumulated.

optimized.idea: Two sweeps, no extra arrays. The first sweep fills answer[i] with the product of everything strictly to the left of i — answer[0] is 1 because nothing is to the left of index 0. The second sweep walks backwards carrying a single running suffix product in a variable and multiplies it into each slot before folding nums[i] into it. Each answer[i] therefore ends up as left product times right product.
code: answer[i] = answer[i - 1] * nums[i - 1];   // product of everything strictly LEFT of i

commonMistakes: Computing the total product and dividing it by nums[i]: quite apart from being banned, [1,2,0,4] throws ArithmeticException at index 2, and the usual patch — count the zeros and special-case one of them — still returns the wrong answer for two zeros unless that case is special-cased as well.

Writing answer[i] = suffix in the backward sweep instead of answer[i] *= suffix: the prefix pass is silently thrown away and the output becomes a pure suffix-product array, which is right at index 0 and wrong at every other index — so [1,2,3,4] comes back [24,12,4,1].

Forgetting answer[0] = 1 and relying on Java's default: the prefix sweep then multiplies forward from 0, every slot becomes 0, and the output is all zeros — which looks convincingly like a zero somewhere in the input rather than an uninitialised sentinel.
